bear_case: TSMC's 36% Q2 revenue surge is the strongest foundry-level AI demand signal available Monday morning — and it makes the STEP ASIDE call uncomfortable. If AI infrastructure capex is running at full speed (June foundry revenue +68% YoY), then Iran noise is a multiple headwind, not a demand headwind, and NVDA's $250 Aug-26 target is simply a matter of CPI timing. The problem with this bull framing is the oil trajectory: WTI at $73-74 is only 8-9% below the $80 September-hike trip wire, and Iran is now conducting offensive military strikes on US facilities in five countries simultaneously while claiming Hormuz is closed. The Red Sea crisis precedent (Q1 2024) showed that oil markets can reprice 15-20% in 2-3 weeks when a choke point is actively contested with sustained military force. A WTI move from $74 to $80 before July 17 converts the August CPI into a structural shock and re-prices the entire July 14 CPI result as a false anchor. BTC at $62,953 with a 24h low of $62,489 — $489 above Gate 2 — is the crypto market's verdict on this scenario: it is pricing the macro risk honestly. If BTC closes below $62,000 tonight, the mandatory defensive adjustment protocol overrides everything else regardless of TSMC, SKHY, or CPI consensus. Counter-argument: if SPX holds 7,460 (dual-gate floor) through Monday's close, VIX stays below 17, BTC holds $62,000, and WTI fails to sustain above $74, then Tuesday's CPI binary is the dominant catalyst and today's STEP ASIDE was correct risk management for the right period. Invalidation: SPX closes Monday above 7,575 with VIX below 16 and BTC above $63,500 → reassess to HOLD or BUY by Tuesday's pre-open.
